title: Integrating technology into teaching under CBE: a low-cost approach
description: A practical guide for Kenyan school principals on using technology to support teaching and learning in ways that fit limited budgets and unreliable connectivity.
body:
Technology in schools is often discussed as if it needs a computer lab and fast internet. Many Kenyan schools have neither, and that does not mean technology cannot help. The smarter approach is to start with a teaching problem and look for the simplest tool that solves it.

Small, well-chosen steps usually do more than large purchases that sit unused.

Start with the problem, not the device

Ask where teachers lose the most time or where students struggle most. If entering and compiling marks takes days, that is a problem technology can fix cheaply. If science students cannot see experiments, a teacher's phone and a short clip may help.

Low-cost wins

  • Digital attendance and results entry, which saves teacher time immediately.
  • A single projector or a teacher's phone used for demonstrations, images, and short videos.
  • Offline resources downloaded in advance, so lessons do not depend on live internet.
  • Messaging tools used carefully for notices and homework reminders, with clear boundaries on hours.

Measure whether it helps: After a term, ask whether the tool saved time, improved results, or engaged students more. If not, stop using it. Technology is only worth keeping if it makes something better.

Set a clear device policy

Decide what students may and may not do with phones and other devices at school, and apply it consistently. A clear policy, explained to students and parents, avoids both blanket bans that get ignored and open use that disrupts lessons.

Build teacher confidence

Teachers who are not confident with technology will avoid it. Short, practical, hands-on sessions, ideally led by a colleague who already uses a tool well, work better than formal lectures.

Teach online safety

Students need to understand privacy, respectful online conduct, and how to spot scams and harmful content. Include this in guidance sessions.

Start with the technology that saves time today.
